senses.whyHard: Not the usual meaning! Usually: wind is moving air.

wine.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wing.whyHard: A common word with more than one meaning. Check the meaning here.

senses.meaning: A group of dragons (or planes) flying together.
senses.whyHard: Not the usual meaning! Usually: The part of a bird's or dragon's body used for flying.

anchors.context: Glory turned and saw a wing of dragons flying high up

wingbeat.meaning: One movement of a wing up and down.
wingbeat.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

wink.meaning: To close one eye quickly, as a friendly sign or a joke.
wink.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.
wink.example: He winked at me and smiled.

wipe.meaning: To clean something by moving a cloth over it.
wipe.usageNote: A common word. Good to learn.

senses.meaning: "Wipe out" = to remove or destroy all of something.
senses.whyHard: A common word with more than one meaning. Check the meaning here.

wiry.meaning: (Of hair or fur) stiff and rough, like wire.
wiry.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.
wiry.example: The dog had wiry brown fur.

wistful.meaning: A little sad because you want something you cannot have. "Wistfully" = in this way.
wistful.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

wistfully.meaning: In a sad way, wishing for something you cannot have.
wistfully.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.
wistfully.example: She looked wistfully at the toys.

wit.meaning: The ability to say clever and funny things quickly.
wit.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

withdraw.meaning: To pull back; to take something away.
withdraw.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

withstand.meaning: To stay strong and not be hurt by something.
withstand.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.
withstand.example: IceWings can withstand very cold weather.

witness.meaning: A "witness" is a person who sees something happen.
witness.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wobble.meaning: To shake from side to side.
wobble.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

woefully.meaning: In a very sad way; or very badly.
woefully.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

wooden.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.
wooden.example: We sat on a wooden bench.

senses.whyHard: Not the usual meaning! Usually: a word is a unit of language, like "cat" or "run".

worthwhile.meaning: Worth the time or effort; useful.

worthy.meaning: Good enough to have or get something.
worthy.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wow.meaning: A word you say when you are very surprised or think something is great.
wow.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wrap.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wrapping.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wreath.meaning: A ring of flowers or leaves. "Wreathing" = going around something like a ring.
wreath.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.
wreath.example: She wore a wreath of flowers.

wreck.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wrestle.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wriggle.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

writhe.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

wry.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

yank.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

yell.usageNote: A common word. Good to understand.

yowl.usageNote: You only need to understand it for this story.

paragraphs.context: Queen: Since the death of Queen Oasis, the tribe is split between
paragraphs.mainIdea: Three sisters want to be queen.
paragraphs.simple: Queen Oasis of the SandWings died. Now her three daughters, Burn, Blister and Blaze, all want her throne.

background.note: Queen Oasis was the SandWing queen before the war. After she died, her three daughters fought over her throne.
Burn is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is huge and violent.
Blister is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is clever and cold.
Blaze is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is friendly but not very clever.

paragraphs.context: Alliances: Burn fights alongside SkyWings and MudWings; Blister is allied with the
paragraphs.simple: Each SandWing sister has friends in other tribes. Burn has the SkyWings and MudWings, Blister has the SeaWings, and Blaze has the IceWings.

background.note: The desert dragons of Pyrrhia. They have pale gold scales and a poisonous barb on the end of the tail, and they can live a long time without water.
Silver-white or pale blue dragons from the frozen north of Pyrrhia. They can live in great cold and breathe out a deadly freezing breath (frostbreath).

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire (if warm enough), hold their breath for up
paragraphs.simple: MudWings can breathe fire when they are warm, stay under water or mud for an hour without breathing, and hide in mud. They are very strong.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: powerful fighters and fliers, can breathe fire
paragraphs.simple: SkyWings are strong fighters and fast fliers, and they can breathe fire.

paragraphs.context: Description: blue or green or aquamarine scales; webs between their claws; gills
paragraphs.simple: SeaWings are blue or green. They have skin between their claws, gills for breathing under water, and stripes that glow in the dark.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can withstand subzero temperatures and bright light, exhale a deadly freezing breath
paragraphs.simple: IceWings can live in very cold places and bright light, and they breathe out a deadly freezing breath.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can camouflage their scales to blend into their surroundings, use their
paragraphs.simple: RainWings can change the colors of their scales to hide and can hold on to branches with their tails. The guide says they have no natural weapons.

paragraphs.context: Abilities: can breathe fire, disappear into dark shadows, read minds, foretell the future
paragraphs.simple: NightWings breathe fire and hide in shadows. People say they can read minds and see the future.

background.note: The power to hear what other dragons are thinking. Many dragons believe NightWings have this power.

paragraphs.context: When the war has lasted twenty years . . .
paragraphs.simple: This is the Dragonet Prophecy. Its first lines say that the dragonets will come when the war has gone on for twenty years.

background.note: The old prophecy that says five dragonets hatched on the brightest night will end the war.

paragraphs.context: When the land is soaked in blood and tears . . .
paragraphs.mainIdea: A land full of blood and tears.
paragraphs.simple: The dragonets will also come when the land is full of blood and tears: when many dragons have died and many are sad.

paragraphs.context: Find the SeaWing egg of deepest blue.
paragraphs.simple: These lines tell which eggs to find. One is a dark blue SeaWing egg. "Wings of night" means that a NightWing dragonet will come too.

paragraphs.context: The largest egg in mountain high
paragraphs.simple: The biggest egg, from high in the mountains, will give a SkyWing ("wings of sky").

paragraphs.context: For wings of earth, search through the mud
paragraphs.simple: For a MudWing ("wings of earth"), look in the mud for a red egg, the color of dragon blood.

paragraphs.context: And hidden alone from the rival queens,
paragraphs.simple: A SandWing egg is waiting, hidden where the SandWing queens who fight each other cannot find it.

paragraphs.context: Of three queens who blister and blaze and burn,
paragraphs.simple: Three SandWing sisters want to be queen. Two of them will die. "Blister and blaze and burn" are words for burning, and also the names of the sisters.

background.note: Blister is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is clever and cold.
Blaze is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is friendly but not very clever.
Burn is one of three SandWing sisters who are fighting to be queen. She is huge and violent.

paragraphs.context: if she bows to a fate that is stronger and higher,
paragraphs.simple: The sister who lives will learn this: if she accepts a fate that is stronger and higher than her, she will have great power, the "wings of fire".

paragraphs.context: Five eggs to hatch on brightest night,
paragraphs.mainIdea: Five eggs on the brightest night.
paragraphs.simple: Five eggs will hatch on the brightest night, and the five dragons will be born to end the war.

background.note: A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: Bright scales in green and red and gold caught the rising sun
paragraphs.simple: Five young dragons are fighting on top of a cliff by the sea in the early morning. They hiss and bite, and the sea crashes on the sand below.

paragraphs.context: It was embarrassing, was what it was. Nautilus glanced up uneasily at
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus is standing next to Morrowseer, a huge black NightWing. The dragonets have not even noticed them. Nautilus knows Morrowseer is surely reading his mind.

background.note: Nautilus is the SeaWing leader of the Talons of Peace.
Morrowseer is a big, scary NightWing. Years ago he told the Talons of Peace about the Dragonet Prophecy.

paragraphs.context: He also wished there were more Talons of Peace around, but when
paragraphs.simple: When the other Talons of Peace heard that the NightWing was coming, most of them suddenly found important jobs somewhere else. Their hiding place in the sea cliffs is almost empty.

background.note: A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: But apparently no one had seen fit to warn the objects of
paragraphs.simple: No one thought it was a good idea to tell the five dragonets that Morrowseer was coming to look at them closely.

paragraphs.context: “I can see that.” Morrowseer’s dark eyes narrowed as Viper, the SandWing,
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer watches as Viper falls into a crack in the rock, Ochre trips and lands on top of her, and Viper bites his tail.

background.note: Viper is a young SandWing. The Talons of Peace raised her as a 'backup' dragonet.
Ochre is a young MudWing dragonet who lives with the Talons of Peace.

paragraphs.context: Flame, the red SkyWing dragonet, snapped his mouth shut and whipped his
paragraphs.simple: Flame shuts his mouth and looks around. Morrowseer steps into the sunlight and looks down at them like a proud king.

background.note: Flame is a young SkyWing dragonet who lives with the Talons of Peace.

paragraphs.context: “I knew it!” crowed the little NightWing dragonet. Fatespeaker leaped off a
paragraphs.simple: The little NightWing, Fatespeaker, says she knew that a NightWing was coming. She is proud, because she thinks she can see the future.

background.note: Fatespeaker is a cheerful young NightWing who lives with the Talons of Peace. She believes she can see the future.

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer flicked his tongue out and in, considering. “It is clear to
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says it was a mistake to let the Talons of Peace look after the dragonets of the prophecy, both the real ones and the false ones.

background.note: A message that tells what will happen in the future. NightWings who can see the future give prophecies.

paragraphs.context: “Right,” said Nautilus. “Basically right. So the prophecy says that five dragonets
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus explains the prophecy to Squid: five dragonets from five tribes, hatched about six years ago, will end the war and choose the next SandWing queen.

background.note: Squid is a young SeaWing dragonet who lives with the Talons of Peace.

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer glanced back at Fatespeaker, the NightWing dragonet. She was sitting on
paragraphs.simple: Fatespeaker is leaning so far forward to listen that she looks like she will soon lose her balance and fall off her stone column.

paragraphs.context: “We gave up worldly things to fight for a higher cause,” Nautilus
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus says the Talons gave up rich things to fight for something more important: peace.

paragraphs.context: “I foresee that I am going to regret this,” said Morrowseer, frowning
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says he will train the prophecy dragonets himself now. They have been handled badly for too long and need clearer direction.

paragraphs.context: “What does that mean?” Nautilus asked. A sense of dread was starting
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus starts to feel a cold fear. He worries that Morrowseer will hurt Squid, and that Squid's mother will be very angry with him.

paragraphs.context: “Three moons,” Morrowseer said with disgust. “This dragonet is your son.”
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer reads Nautilus's mind and finds his secret: Squid is Nautilus's own son.

background.note: The dragon world has three moons. Dragons say 'Three moons!' when they are surprised or upset, the way people say 'Oh my goodness!'

paragraphs.context: Nautilus stared down at his claws. It had seemed like a good
paragraphs.simple: The Talons decided to have backup dragonets. Squid hatched at about the right time, though not on the brightest night, and everyone treated him as very special.

background.note: A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: “Of course I am,” said Squid. “Isn’t that a funny coincidence? Wow.
paragraphs.simple: Squid is proud to be the leader's son and a dragonet of destiny. He walks off proudly. The others will probably burn his snout again soon.

background.note: The five dragonets of the prophecy are called the dragonets of destiny. 'Destiny' means what is sure to happen in the future.

paragraphs.context: Nautilus watched him go, wondering how everything had gone so wrong. Why
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus wonders why the Talons worked with Morrowseer and how they lost the real dragonets. That question makes him very upset.

paragraphs.context: Kestrel, Dune, and Webs should have been able to keep a handle
paragraphs.simple: The guardians should have controlled the five real dragonets, but the dragonets escaped. Since then they may have killed Queen Scarlet, caused trouble in the Sky Kingdom, turned Queen Coral against her friends and wrecked the SeaWing palace.

background.note: Kestrel was a SkyWing guardian who raised the dragonets. She was strict and fierce.
Dune was a SandWing guardian who raised the dragonets.
Webs is a SeaWing from the Talons of Peace. He was one of the dragonets' guardians.
Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.
Queen Coral is the queen of the SeaWings and Tsunami's mother.
The large land (continent) where all the dragon tribes in these books live.

paragraphs.context: Nautilus blanched. Do their parents count as “witnesses”? he wondered before he
paragraphs.simple: Nautilus goes pale. He wonders if the parents would be called witnesses too, and then tries to stop the thought quickly, before Morrowseer reads it.

paragraphs.context: “We’ll cross that bridge when we come to it,” Morrowseer said briskly.
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says they will deal with that later. They do not know yet which dragonets they will use and which they will throw away.
hardWords: cross that bridge when we come to it

paragraphs.context: Morrowseer snorted. “Very well. I’ll try to bring yours back in one
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer promises to bring Squid back safe. Then he reminds Nautilus that the Talons always say anything must be given up to end the war.

paragraphs.context: “The alternate dragonets were your idea in the first place. A good
paragraphs.simple: Morrowseer says the real dragonets have not been good enough. His plan: get rid of the most dangerous ones and train the backup dragonets to take their places.

paragraphs.context: She most certainly did not love this weather.
paragraphs.simple: Glory grew up in caves, so she has never been in rain before. Five days of rain make her wet, heavy and unhappy.

paragraphs.context: Three moons, please let them be sensible dragons.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Glory hopes the RainWings are sensible.
paragraphs.simple: "Three moons" is a dragon way of saying "Oh my goodness". Glory hopes the RainWings are not like the stories about them.

background.note: The dragon world has three moons. Dragons say 'Three moons!' when they are surprised or upset, the way people say 'Oh my goodness!'

paragraphs.context: Everyone said RainWings were useless and lazy.
paragraphs.simple: Other dragons say RainWings are useless and lazy. But nobody really sees them in their rainforest, so the stories may be wrong.

background.note: Dragons of the rainforest whose scales change colour. They can hide by matching the colours around them, and they can shoot venom from their fangs.
The thick, hot, wet forest in Pyrrhia where the RainWings live. The books call the RainWings' home 'the rainforest'.

paragraphs.context: Glory narrowed her eyes at him as the blue-green dragon flopped
paragraphs.simple: Webs is hurt, so the dragonets walk instead of flying. He keeps asking to stop, and Glory thinks he does not want to reach the rainforest.

background.note: Glory is a RainWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She can change the colour of her scales and shoot venom.
Webs is a SeaWing from the Talons of Peace. He was one of the dragonets' guardians.

paragraphs.context: Clay paced over to Webs and peered down at his wound.
paragraphs.simple: A SandWing poison scratch near Webs's tail is turning black and spreading. The dragonets do not know how to fight this poison.

background.note: Clay is a MudWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is big, kind and loyal.

paragraphs.context: Not to mention we have no idea why Blister wanted Webs dead so badly.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Why did Blister want Webs dead?
paragraphs.simple: Glory wonders why Blister wanted to kill Webs. She looks at Starflight, the cleverest dragonet she knows.

background.note: Starflight is a NightWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. He is shy and very clever, and he loves reading scrolls.
Purple-black dragons with silver scales under their wings, like a night sky full of stars. Many dragons believe they can read minds and see the future.

paragraphs.context: Stealing her egg had been his idea, too.
paragraphs.simple: The prophecy wanted a SkyWing. When that egg was lost, Webs took a RainWing egg instead, so Glory grew up far from home in a prophecy with no place for her.

background.note: A message that tells what will happen in the future. NightWings who can see the future give prophecies.
A secret group of dragons from different tribes who want to end the war. They raised the dragonets of the prophecy.

paragraphs.context: Rolls of thick gray fog hung over the mud, wreathing the stunted
paragraphs.simple: Gray fog covers the swamp and the rain never stops. It is almost impossible to see anything.

background.note: Tsunami is a SeaWing princess, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is brave and likes to be the leader.

paragraphs.context: “We should still hide,” Starflight said anxiously.
paragraphs.simple: Starflight warns that they are only one day's flight from the MudWing queen's palace, so they must hide.

background.note: Queen Moorhen is the queen of the MudWings.

paragraphs.context: Every queen they’d met so far seemed determined to keep the dragonets
paragraphs.mainIdea: Every queen wants to trap them.
paragraphs.simple: Every queen they have met wants to keep the dragonets as prisoners. They escaped from Queen Scarlet only because Glory found she could shoot venom.

background.note: Queen Scarlet was the cruel queen of the SkyWings until she lost her throne. She liked to watch prisoners fight in her arena.
The land of the SkyWings, high in the mountains.
Poison made by an animal. RainWings can shoot venom from their fangs that melts whatever it hits; SandWings have poison in the barb on their tail.

paragraphs.context: After that escape they’d gone looking for safety with Tsunami’s mother, Queen
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami's mother locked them up too.
paragraphs.simple: Next they went to Tsunami's mother, Queen Coral of the SeaWings, but she also locked them up. Everyone has their own plan for the war.

background.note: Queen Coral is the queen of the SeaWings and Tsunami's mother.

paragraphs.context: The MudWing queen held court beside a large lake on the southern
paragraphs.simple: If they are close to the MudWing palace, they must also be close to the rainforest, where Glory's tribe lives.

background.note: The land of the MudWings, full of swamps, lakes and mud.

paragraphs.context: The little SandWing had been unusually quiet for the last few days.
paragraphs.simple: Sunny has been quiet for days. SandWings are made for hot, dry deserts, not rain.

background.note: Sunny is a small SandWing, one of the five dragonets of the prophecy. She is cheerful and always hopes for the best.

paragraphs.context: Clay shepherded Tsunami up next to Webs and spread his mud-colored
paragraphs.simple: Clay hides Tsunami and Webs under his wings. They are not hidden perfectly, but in the fog they look like a pile of mud.

paragraphs.context: “If that were true,” said the first voice, “then Her Majesty would
paragraphs.simple: A MudWing soldier says the queen does not let them hunt in the rainforest because it is not safe. They hear screaming at night.

paragraphs.context: “That’s not some kind of rainforest monster,” said the second guard, but
paragraphs.simple: The other soldier thinks the screaming and dead bodies come from enemy dragons in the war, but she does not sound sure.

paragraphs.context: “Tell me about it.” Tramp-squelch-tramp-squelch. “So what do you
paragraphs.simple: The soldiers talk about the "SkyWing situation": the SkyWings must choose a new queen, and some want Ruby.

background.note: Ruby is a SkyWing dragon. Now that Queen Scarlet has lost her throne, some SkyWings want Ruby to be their new queen.

paragraphs.context: Glory strained her ears, but their voices faded into the mist as
paragraphs.simple: Glory wants to know what is happening with the SkyWings, so she quietly follows the two MudWing soldiers.

paragraphs.context: Glory’s ruff flared in fear and pale green stripes zigzagged through her scales.
paragraphs.simple: A scream makes Glory afraid, and fear shows in her scales. She forces them back to gray and brown so she stays hidden.

paragraphs.context: Two brown dragons were sprawled in the mud, surrounded by pools of
paragraphs.simple: Glory finds the two MudWings dead in the mud. Something has torn out their throats.

paragraphs.context: “IceWings! Yes!” Clay said. “That sounds like a great plan. Let’s do
paragraphs.simple: Clay wants to go to the Ice Kingdom instead, where there are no strange dragon-killers. He talks nervously about fighting penguins.

background.note: The cold, snowy land of the IceWings in the far north.

paragraphs.context: The gnarled claw shapes of the marsh trees were half a day
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami wanted to look for clues, but the others did not want to be caught near two dead soldiers. They all flew through the night.

paragraphs.context: Warm bursts of sunlight nudged through the leafy canopy, making all their scales glow.
paragraphs.simple: Sunlight comes through the leaves. Glory lets her scales turn beetle green and amber, and she likes matching the trees.

paragraphs.context: We’ll be there soon, she thought with a shiver of anticipation.
paragraphs.mainIdea: Glory hopes for a better home.
paragraphs.simple: Glory tells herself not to hope too much. Anything will be better than the cave where the guardians hated her.

paragraphs.context: “All right, enough. What do you know about this?” she demanded. “You’re
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami holds Webs by the snout and asks him what he knows about a monster in the rainforest.

paragraphs.context: “I swear I don’t know anything about a monster,” he said.
paragraphs.simple: Webs says he saw nothing dangerous when he stole Glory's egg. It was the night before the brightest night, and no RainWing stopped him.

background.note: A night when all three moons are full at the same time. The prophecy says the five dragonets will hatch on the brightest night.

paragraphs.context: That doesn’t mean anything, Glory thought, but she remembered the MudWing village
paragraphs.simple: Glory remembers that Clay's mother sold his egg for two cows and did not want him back. She hopes her own parents are not like that.

paragraphs.context: Well, Glory didn’t particularly care whether her parents were the most amazing
paragraphs.simple: Glory does not need perfect parents. She wants to show her friends that RainWings are not just lazy fruit-eaters.

paragraphs.context: Glory knew that. She’d memorized every reference she could find anywhere to
paragraphs.mainIdea: What Glory knows about the rainforest.
paragraphs.simple: Glory read every scroll about RainWings, but they said almost nothing. One scroll told her about quicksand, poisonous snakes and deadly bugs.

background.note: A long roll of paper with writing on it. Dragons keep their books, maps and letters as scrolls.

paragraphs.context: Glory wasn’t hungry anymore, now that the sun had finally come out.
paragraphs.simple: In the sun Glory is not hungry. She feels a little guilty remembering how Queen Scarlet showed her off on a tree like treasure.

paragraphs.context: But I didn’t love it, Glory told herself fiercely.
paragraphs.simple: Glory says she did not love being Scarlet's pet. It was just another prison, and she is more than a pretty object.

paragraphs.context: “At least I told you about them,” Glory said, her ruff flaring.
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami says they are jumpy because of the dead bodies. Glory reminds her that Tsunami once hid a dead body from them.

paragraphs.context: “GUYS!” Starflight yelled. They stopped and looked back at him. He was
paragraphs.simple: While they argue, Starflight notices that Sunny is gone.

paragraphs.context: Glory closed her eyes and ransacked her brain.
paragraphs.simple: Glory thinks about the dangers from the scroll: snakes, ants, quicksand. But she sees no quicksand here.

parts.meaning: from what she could see,

parts.text: she was the only RainWing willing to use her venom on other living things.
parts.meaning: she was the one RainWing ready to use venom on living creatures.

sentences.grammar: "As far as she could tell" means "from what she knew". "Willing to + verb" means ready to do something.

sentences.context: She couldn’t have known how long she’d have to fly when she first jumped into the darkness, looking for other prisoners.
sentences.simple: When Kinkajou jumped into the dark to look for other prisoners, she could not know how far she would have to fly.
sentences.main: She couldn’t have known how long she’d have to fly.

parts.text: She couldn’t have known
parts.meaning: It was impossible for her to know

parts.text: how long she’d have to fly
parts.meaning: how long she would need to fly

parts.text: when she first jumped into the darkness,
parts.meaning: when she jumped into the dark the first time,

parts.text: looking for other prisoners.
parts.meaning: to look for other prisoners.

sentences.grammar: "Couldn't have known" means it was impossible to know in the past. "She'd" here is "she would". "Looking for ..." tells what she was doing.

sentences.context: Glory didn’t have to look back; she’d already heard the wingbeats, and she didn’t really want to know exactly how many NightWings were on their tails.
sentences.simple: Glory did not need to look behind her. She had heard the wings, and she did not want to know how many NightWings were following them.
sentences.main: Glory didn’t have to look back.

parts.text: Glory didn’t have to look back;
parts.meaning: Glory did not need to look behind her;

parts.text: she’d already heard the wingbeats,
parts.meaning: she had already heard the sound of wings,

parts.text: and she didn’t really want to know exactly how many NightWings were on their tails.
parts.meaning: and she did not want to know how many NightWings were chasing them.

sentences.grammar: A semicolon (;) joins two closely linked sentences. "On their tails" is an idiom that means following close behind them.

sentences.context: She tried not to think about how much bigger than her Magnificent was, or how many years older she must be.
sentences.simple: Glory tried not to think about how much larger and older Magnificent was than her.
sentences.main: She tried not to think about it.

parts.text: She tried not to think about
parts.meaning: She tried to not think about

parts.text: how much bigger than her Magnificent was,
parts.meaning: how much larger Magnificent was than her,

parts.text: or how many years older she must be.
parts.meaning: or how much older she surely was.

sentences.grammar: "Try not to + verb" means try to avoid doing something. "How much bigger" and "how many years older" are question words used inside a sentence. "Must be" means "surely is".

sentences.context: Most of the dragons looked confused, but a few had dark purple stripes rippling over their scales — guilt and shame, living right next to pride on the color spectrum.
sentences.simple: Most dragons looked confused, but some had dark purple stripes. That color means guilt and shame, which are close to pride among RainWing colors.
sentences.main: A few had dark purple stripes.

parts.text: Most of the dragons looked confused,
parts.meaning: Most dragons looked puzzled,

parts.text: but a few had dark purple stripes rippling over their scales
parts.meaning: but some had dark purple lines moving over their scales

parts.text: — guilt and shame,
parts.meaning: — a color of feeling bad about what they did,

parts.text: living right next to pride on the color spectrum.
parts.meaning: very close to the color of pride.

sentences.grammar: The dash explains what the purple means. "Rippling" and "living" are -ing words that describe the nouns before them.

sentences.context: Whenever she felt her brain getting tired, she’d think of the smoky air choking the caves of the RainWings, and that would snap her back into focus.
sentences.simple: Every time she felt tired, she thought of the smoky caves where the RainWings were held, and that made her concentrate again.
sentences.main: She’d think of the smoky air.

parts.text: Whenever she felt her brain getting tired,
parts.meaning: Every time she felt her mind getting tired,

parts.text: she’d think of the smoky air choking the caves of the RainWings,
parts.meaning: she would think of the smoke filling the prisoners' caves,

parts.text: and that would snap her back into focus.
parts.meaning: and that would quickly make her pay attention again.

sentences.grammar: "Whenever" means "every time". Here "she'd" and "would" mean she did this many times in the past. "Snap back into focus" means suddenly concentrate again.

sentences.context: Behind Scarlet she caught a glimpse of a dim room with glass jars hanging from the ceiling, some of them glowing strangely.
sentences.simple: Behind Scarlet, Glory quickly saw a dark room. Glass jars hung from the ceiling, and some of them were glowing in a strange way.
sentences.main: She caught a glimpse of a dim room.

parts.text: Behind Scarlet
parts.meaning: Behind Scarlet

parts.text: she caught a glimpse of a dim room
parts.meaning: she saw a dark room for a moment

parts.text: with glass jars hanging from the ceiling,
parts.meaning: with glass jars hanging from the top,

parts.text: some of them glowing strangely.
parts.meaning: and some of them gave off a strange light.

sentences.grammar: "Catch a glimpse of" means see something for a very short time. "Some of them glowing ..." is a short phrase with no main verb that adds a detail.

sentences.context: Her scales kept shifting to match the dark green leaves below them, as if she was trying to hide whatever she was really feeling.
sentences.simple: Kinkajou's scales kept turning the color of the dark leaves, as if she wanted to hide her real feelings.
sentences.main: Her scales kept shifting.

parts.text: Her scales kept shifting
parts.meaning: Her scales kept changing

parts.text: to match the dark green leaves below them,
parts.meaning: to be the same color as the dark leaves under them,

parts.text: as if she was trying to hide whatever she was really feeling.
parts.meaning: as if she wanted to hide her true feelings.

sentences.grammar: "Kept + -ing" means did again and again. "As if" tells how it looked. "Whatever she was really feeling" means "any feeling that she really had".

sentences.context: Queen Scarlet and Queen Coral preferred to have their minions do their dirty work, but Burn and Blister both seemed rather claws-on.
sentences.simple: Scarlet and Coral liked to make their servants do the bad jobs, but Burn and Blister seemed to do things themselves.
sentences.main: Scarlet and Coral preferred to have their minions do their dirty work.

parts.text: Queen Scarlet and Queen Coral preferred
parts.meaning: Queen Scarlet and Queen Coral liked

parts.text: to have their minions do their dirty work,
parts.meaning: to make their servants do the unpleasant jobs,

parts.text: but Burn and Blister both seemed rather claws-on.
parts.meaning: but Burn and Blister seemed to do things with their own claws.

sentences.grammar: "Have someone do something" means make someone do it for you. "Claws-on" is a dragon joke on "hands-on", which means doing things yourself.

sentences.context: Kinkajou collapsed in a ball of scales that went instantly white with pain, except for the three spots where black venom was eating through her wing.
sentences.simple: Kinkajou fell down and curled up. Her scales turned white with pain at once, but three spots on her wing were black where the venom was burning.
sentences.main: Kinkajou collapsed in a ball of scales.

parts.text: Kinkajou collapsed in a ball of scales
parts.meaning: Kinkajou fell down and curled into a ball

parts.text: that went instantly white with pain,
parts.meaning: and her scales turned white with pain at once,

parts.text: except for the three spots where black venom was eating through her wing.
parts.meaning: but not three spots where black venom was burning through her wing.

sentences.grammar: "That went white" is a relative clause about the scales. "Except for" means "not including". "Was eating through" (past continuous) shows the venom still working.

sentences.context: She had never ever imagined that the Night Kingdom — her kingdom — would be so dark and smelly and that all the dragons here would be so incredibly cranky.
sentences.simple: Fatespeaker never thought the Night Kingdom, her own home, would be so dark and smelly, or that the dragons would be so bad-tempered.
sentences.main: She had never imagined that the Night Kingdom would be so dark.

parts.text: She had never ever imagined
parts.meaning: She had never once thought

parts.text: that the Night Kingdom — her kingdom — would be so dark and smelly
parts.meaning: that the Night Kingdom, her own home, would be so dark and smelly

parts.text: and that all the dragons here would be so incredibly cranky.
parts.meaning: and that the dragons there would be so bad-tempered.

sentences.grammar: Two "that" clauses tell what she imagined. "Would be" is the future seen from the past. "Never ever" is a strong way to say "never".

sentences.context: Is that all I’m good for — all any RainWing is
sentences.simple: Glory asks if sleeping in the sun is the only thing she is good for, and the only thing any RainWing is good for.
sentences.grammar: She asks the same question twice. The second time it is about every RainWing, not only herself.

sentences.context: gotten there first, gone through to this place, warned these
sentences.simple: Glory guesses that Deathbringer reached the tunnel first, warned the dragons there, and then went back.
sentences.grammar: One long line of guesses, joined by and and then, so each step has to be held until the end.

sentences.context: it pulsed with such a feeling of not-supposed-to-be-there that she
sentences.simple: The hole in the tree feels so wrong that Glory wants to look away as soon as she sees it.
sentences.grammar: The words not-supposed-to-be-there are stuck together as one feeling, and that feeling is why she wants to look away.
